Paper Title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
Authors: Lingjiao Chen; Matei Zaharia; James Zou
Problem: Reduce LLM inference cost without sacrificing task quality.
Dataset / Task Setting: Multiple LLM APIs; classification, QA, and reasoning tasks.
Method: Learns LLM cascades, ordering models and stopping thresholds using quality/cost estimates.
Key Findings: Cascades can retain or improve quality while substantially reducing cost; final TMLR publication is 2024.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Primarily cost-quality optimisation; does not estimate separate residual failure risk for repair vs independent regeneration after observing an SLM answer.
Relevance to TRACER: Foundational cascade baseline; supports learned stopping/escalation decisions.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER differs by post-response tri-action risk estimation rather than cascade order/cost optimisation.

Paper Title: Hybrid LLM: Cost-Efficient and Quality-Aware Query Routing
Problem: Choose between cheaper and stronger LLMs while controlling quality/cost.
Dataset / Task Setting: Query-level model routing before candidate generation.
Method: Predicts query difficulty/quality to select a weak or strong model.
Key Findings: Learned query routing can reduce expensive-model usage while maintaining quality.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Decision is made before seeing the SLM response; cannot use response-specific failure evidence.
Relevance to TRACER: Strong pre-generation routing baseline.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER conditions risk on the actual initial response and estimates three action outcomes.

Paper Title: Large Language Model Cascades with Mixture of Thought Representations for Cost-Efficient Reasoning
Problem: Use consistency signals to decide whether reasoning should escalate to stronger models.
Dataset / Task Setting: Reasoning tasks in cascaded LLM inference.
Method: Mixture-of-thought representations and consistency signals for cascade decisions.
Metrics / Evaluation: Reasoning accuracy, model usage, inference cost.
Key Findings: Post-generation signals can improve cost-efficient cascade decisions.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Escalation is not decomposed into repair and independent regeneration with separate calibrated residual risks.
Relevance to TRACER: Evidence that output-derived signals are valuable after generation.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER generalises post-generation escalation into distinct action-conditional risks.

Paper Title: AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models
Problem: Decide whether to accept a small-model answer or escalate to a larger model.
Dataset / Task Setting: Small model answers first; router uses approximate correctness/self-verification.
Method: Few-shot self-verification plus POMDP-based accept/escalate policy.
Key Findings: Output-aware verification can support efficient accept-or-escalate decisions.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Binary action space and intrinsic/self-verification signal; no separate repair vs independent regeneration risks.
Relevance to TRACER: Closest conceptual predecessor to TRACER.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER separates escalation into REPAIR and REGENERATE and calibrates residual failure per action.

Paper Title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
Problem: Learn model selection between weak and strong LLMs from preference data.
Dataset / Task Setting: Pre-generation multi-model routing.
Method: Preference-based routers predicting which model should handle a query.
Metrics / Evaluation: Quality-cost trade-off and generalisation across datasets/model pairs.
Key Findings: Learned routers can transfer and significantly reduce strong-model calls.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Does not observe the initial SLM response before routing and does not model repair.
Relevance to TRACER: Modern learned-router baseline and evaluation reference.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER is response-conditioned and action-conditioned rather than query-only model selection.

Paper Title: A Unified Approach to Routing and Cascading for LLMs
Problem: Unify routing and cascading under common performance/cost optimisation.
Dataset / Task Setting: Multi-LLM selection and cascade policies.
Method: Unified mathematical framework driven by model-quality estimates.
Key Findings: Routing and cascading can be understood through common quality-estimation principles.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Optimisation target is not TRACER's three post-response residual failure probabilities.
Relevance to TRACER: Theoretical foundation for comparing router action spaces and quality estimators.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER defines actions over outcomes of one initial response rather than only model-selection sequences.

Paper Title: Learning to Route LLMs with Confidence Tokens
Problem: Improve LLM routing by learning specialised confidence representations.
Dataset / Task Setting: Confidence-aware routing/rejection.
Method: Trains confidence tokens to represent routing-relevant uncertainty.
Key Findings: Learned confidence representations can outperform simpler probability signals.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Confidence signal is not itself a calibrated action-conditional residual-failure model.
Relevance to TRACER: Supports learned uncertainty features for ACRE.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER calibrates probabilities for each downstream action, not a single confidence/routing score.

Paper Title: SATER: A Self-Aware and Token-Efficient Approach to Routing and Cascading
Problem: Reduce redundant generation and strong-model use in routing/cascading.
Dataset / Task Setting: Pre-routing and cascading with self-aware/token-efficient outputs.
Method: Combines self-awareness with token-efficient cascade decisions.
Key Findings: Joint routing/cascading design can reduce unnecessary generation.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Primary aim is efficiency; does not estimate ACCEPT/REPAIR/REGENERATE residual failure separately.
Relevance to TRACER: Important efficiency comparison even though TRACER treats cost/latency as secondary.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER's primary objective is residual failure risk rather than token/cost minimisation.

Paper Title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
Problem: Improve generated outputs using external tools to critique and revise.
Dataset / Task Setting: Iterative LLM self-correction with tool feedback.
Method: Tool-interactive critique followed by revision.
Key Findings: External feedback can make correction more reliable than unaided self-reflection.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Correction is applied as a procedure, not selected against accept and independent regeneration via calibrated risk.
Relevance to TRACER: Supports validator-assisted REPAIR design.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER decides whether repair is preferable instead of assuming correction should run.

Paper Title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
Problem: Test whether LLMs can reliably improve reasoning through intrinsic self-correction.
Dataset / Task Setting: Reasoning tasks with self-correction prompts.
Method: Controlled empirical evaluation of intrinsic correction.
Key Findings: Unaided self-correction can fail or degrade correct responses.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Focuses on self-correction rather than external stronger-model repair/routing.
Relevance to TRACER: Motivates explicit repair risk and repair-damage measurement.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER allows ACCEPT when repair is predicted riskier and compares repair with independent regeneration.

Paper Title: Small Language Models Need Strong Verifiers to Self-Correct Reasoning
Problem: Understand SLM self-correction and the role of verifier strength.
Dataset / Task Setting: Small language models with verifier feedback.
Method: Compares correction behaviour under verifier strengths.
Key Findings: Stronger verification materially affects SLM correction success.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Does not learn a tri-action policy over accept, repair and regenerate.
Relevance to TRACER: Direct evidence for SLM + stronger-model/validator collaboration.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER models when strong-assisted repair is worth choosing versus independent regeneration.

Paper Title: Factual Confidence of LLMs: On Reliability and Robustness of Current Estimators
Problem: Assess reliability and robustness of factual-confidence estimators for LLMs.
Dataset / Task Setting: Factual QA/confidence estimation under perturbations.
Method: Benchmarks probability- and representation-based confidence estimators.
Key Findings: Confidence estimators vary in reliability and can be unstable under meaning-preserving changes.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Confidence is not a direct downstream-action residual-risk estimate.
Relevance to TRACER: Supports combining multiple uncertainty signals and evaluating calibration carefully.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: ACRE predicts action-specific failure rather than treating confidence as a generic correctness proxy.

Paper Title: DebugBench: Evaluating Debugging Capability of Large Language Models
Problem: Benchmark LLM debugging capability across realistic bug types.
Dataset / Task Setting: Code debugging benchmark across languages/bug categories.
Method: Curated buggy programs paired with reference repairs and evaluation.
Key Findings: Provides structured code-failure tasks suitable for testing repair/regeneration.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Cached data used in the current PoC did not provide executable tests for all samples; objective fixtures must be constructed/verified.
Relevance to TRACER: Primary code-domain dataset candidate.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER uses benchmark outcomes as offline action labels rather than relying on textual similarity.

Paper Title: FinQA: A Dataset of Numerical Reasoning over Financial Data
Problem: Evaluate numerical reasoning over financial reports combining text and tables.
Dataset / Task Setting: Financial QA with annotated reasoning programs.
Method: Dataset with questions, evidence, answers and executable reasoning programs.
Key Findings: Enables objective numerical reasoning labels with traceable programs.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Domain-specific financial language and reasoning operations may limit generalisation.
Relevance to TRACER: Primary numerical-domain dataset candidate.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: Provides objective action outcomes needed to train calibrated residual-risk heads.

Paper Title: TAT-QA: A Question Answering Benchmark on a Hybrid of Tabular and Textual Content in Finance
Problem: Evaluate QA requiring hybrid table-text reasoning in financial documents.
Dataset / Task Setting: Financial QA with multiple arithmetic/reasoning operation types.
Method: Hybrid table-text dataset with annotated derivations/answers.
Key Findings: Adds a different hybrid numerical reasoning distribution beyond FinQA.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Optional scope; increases validator/data engineering burden.
Relevance to TRACER: Potential external/generalisation dataset.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: Useful for testing whether calibrated action risk transfers beyond one numerical benchmark.

Paper Title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
Authors: Chuan Guo; Geoff Pleiss; Yu Sun; Kilian Q. Weinberger
Problem: Make predicted probabilities correspond to empirical correctness likelihood.
Dataset / Task Setting: Modern neural networks on classification tasks.
Method: Compares post-hoc calibration methods; introduces temperature scaling as an effective practical baseline.
Key Findings: Modern neural networks can be poorly calibrated; temperature scaling is a strong simple post-hoc method.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Classification setting, not autoregressive LLM action routing.
Relevance to TRACER: Direct methodological foundation for ACRE per-head temperature scaling.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER applies calibration to action-conditional residual-failure probabilities.

Paper Title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
Problem: Optimise predictions jointly with a reject/abstain option.
Dataset / Task Setting: Deep classification/regression selective prediction.
Method: Integrated reject option trained end-to-end under target coverage.
Key Findings: Jointly learned selection can improve risk at a given coverage over confidence-threshold baselines.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Binary predict/reject framing; not generative action selection.
Relevance to TRACER: Foundational selective-risk/coverage concept for TRACER's epsilon policy.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER has three actions and chooses between two remediation actions after ACCEPT is unsafe.

Paper Title: How Can We Know When Language Models Know? On the Calibration of Language Models for Question Answering
Authors: Zhengbao Jiang; Jun Araki; Haibo Ding; Graham Neubig
Problem: Determine whether generative LM confidence corresponds to answer correctness.
Dataset / Task Setting: T5, BART and GPT-2 on QA datasets.
Method: Evaluates and improves LM calibration through fine-tuning and post-hoc modifications.
Key Findings: Raw LM probabilities are substantially miscalibrated; calibration methods improve confidence/correctness correspondence.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Single-answer correctness confidence, not downstream action-conditional risk.
Relevance to TRACER: Direct language-model evidence that confidence requires calibration.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER calibrates failure probability conditioned on each action, not just the initial answer.

Paper Title: Conformal Risk Control
Authors: Anastasios N. Angelopoulos; Stephen Bates; Adam Fisch; Lihua Lei; Tal Schuster
Problem: Control expected monotone losses with finite-sample guarantees.
Dataset / Task Setting: General predictive systems; examples include NLP.
Method: Extends conformal prediction to select a parameter controlling expected risk.
Metrics / Evaluation: Expected risk relative to user-specified level; finite-sample guarantee.
Key Findings: Provides a general framework for controlling expected risk using calibration data.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Requires monotone risk-control structure; not a learned tri-action router by itself.
Relevance to TRACER: Theoretical reference for explicit risk thresholds and calibrated/selective policies.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER learns three residual risks and uses an epsilon policy; formal conformal guarantees are not automatically implied.

Paper Title: Selective Generation for Controllable Language Models
Authors: Minjae Lee; Kyungmin Kim; Taesoo Kim; Sangdon Park
Problem: Apply certified selective prediction ideas to free-form language generation.
Dataset / Task Setting: Open/closed-source generative language models with textual-entailment correctness.
Method: Supervised and semi-supervised selective generation controlling false discovery rate under entailment.
Metrics / Evaluation: FDR under entailment and selection efficiency.
Key Findings: Selective generation can meet desired risk levels with theoretical guarantees using an entailment-based correctness relation.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Controls selection of generated content rather than choosing repair vs independent regeneration.
Relevance to TRACER: Direct generative selective-risk precedent; important for avoiding overclaiming novelty.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER's novelty is action-conditional remediation risk, not selective generation itself.

Paper Title: BEST-Route: Adaptive LLM Routing with Test-Time Optimal Compute
Authors: Dujian Ding; Ankur Mallick; Shaokun Zhang; Chi Wang; Daniel Madrigal; Mirian Del Carmen Hipolito Garcia; Menglin Xia; Laks V. S. Lakshmanan; Qingyun Wu; Victor Rühle
Problem: Choose not only a model but also how many samples to draw under quality/cost requirements.
Dataset / Task Setting: Multi-LLM routing with test-time best-of-n sampling.
Method: Routes by query difficulty and quality thresholds to a model plus response count.
Key Findings: Reports up to 60% cost reduction with less than 1% performance drop.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Action space is model/sample-count allocation before outcome-specific repair; not calibrated residual failure for ACCEPT/REPAIR/REGENERATE.
Relevance to TRACER: Important updated closest work showing modern routers are not merely binary.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: Forces TRACER to state a narrower post-response action-risk contribution.

Paper Title: Conformal Tail Risk Control for Large Language Model Alignment
Authors: Catherine Chen; Jingyan Shen; Zhun Deng; Lihua Lei
Problem: Control severe/tail LLM failures under imperfect automated scoring.
Dataset / Task Setting: Black-box LLM outputs and human-machine scoring misalignment.
Method: Conformal calibration for distortion/tail risk measures using L-statistics.
Key Findings: Provides calibrated guarantees for tail-risk measures despite scorer mismatch.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Alignment/tail-risk calibration, not tri-action routing or response repair.
Relevance to TRACER: Strengthens TRACER's risk-calibration theoretical context.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER predicts per-action ordinary residual failure; it should not imply conformal tail guarantees unless added explicitly.

Paper Title: CAP: Conformalized Abstention Policies for Context-Adaptive Risk Management for LLMs and VLMs
Authors: Sina Tayebati; Divake Kumar; Nastaran Darabi; Dinithi Jayasuriya; Theja Tulabandhula; Ranganath Krishnan; Amit Ranjan Trivedi
Problem: Adapt abstention/risk levels per instance rather than applying one global conformal level.
Dataset / Task Setting: LLMs/VLMs, hallucination detection and selective generation.
Method: Reinforcement-learning policy selects per-instance conformal risk level; includes point prediction, set prediction and abstention.
Metrics / Evaluation: Coverage, hallucination AUROC, AUARC, calibration error.
Key Findings: Maintains target coverage while improving selective-generation/risk-management metrics over static conformal baselines.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Focuses on abstention/risk-level choice, not choosing among repair and independent regeneration outcomes.
Relevance to TRACER: Updated evidence that adaptive risk management can be multi-action, so TRACER gap must be precise.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER's specific contribution is calibrated residual failure for three response-handling actions.

Paper Title: LENS: Latent Precision Inference in Multi-LLM Routing
Authors: Juntao Liu; Lixing Yu; Kun Yue; Zhiwen Tang
Problem: Make routing robust when interaction-derived feedback has unknown/variable precision under logging noise and drift.
Dataset / Task Setting: Multi-LLM routing under task/model distribution shifts.
Method: Probabilistic latent-precision model with posterior utility maximisation and variational inference.
Key Findings: Explicitly modeling feedback precision improves routing, especially under task/model shifts.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Routes among models using feedback signatures; no explicit post-response repair action.
Relevance to TRACER: Very recent evidence on uncertainty in supervision and routing calibration under shift.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER should separate label/validator reliability concerns from its action-conditional risk model.

Paper Title: Resample or Reroute? Budget-Aware Test-Time Model Selection for Large Language Models
Problem: Allocate a per-query budget between resampling the committed model and rerouting to another model under an imperfect verifier.
Dataset / Task Setting: Multi-model test-time selection with multiple samples and noisy verification.
Method: Online marginal-correctness-per-cost allocation between resampling and rerouting.
Metrics / Evaluation: Expected correctness and cost-quality Pareto frontier.
Key Findings: Reported gains depend on verifier quality and benchmark heterogeneity.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Not peer-reviewed as of 2026-08-23; resampling/rerouting is not the same as editing an existing SLM response.
Relevance to TRACER: Extremely close emerging work; must be discussed in novelty analysis.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER's REPAIR explicitly conditions on and edits the existing SLM answer, while REGENERATE independently solves; ACRE estimates each action's residual failure rather than marginal correctness per cost.

Paper Title: RLM-Cascade: Response-Level Speculative Decoding for Cost-Efficient LLM API Serving
Authors: Haifeng Wu; Srinivasan Manoharan; Fangbo Tu; Junhua Zhao; Jian Wan
Problem: Reduce LLM API cost by reusing a cheaper draft response and selectively involving a stronger model at response level.
Dataset / Task Setting: Real-world agentic coding workload plus a small Code/Math/Instruct benchmark as reported by the preprint.
Method: A cheap draft model produces a response; a lightweight complexity router controls whether the draft is used directly, a stronger verifier/model is involved, or the response is enhanced.
Metrics / Evaluation: Draft-use rate, API cost, latency, and task pass rate.
Key Findings: The preprint reports substantial draft reuse, lower cost and latency, and competitive quality in its evaluated workloads.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Preprint only; optimisation is primarily serving efficiency. The abstract does not define separately calibrated residual-failure probabilities for ACCEPT, context-preserving REPAIR, and independent REGENERATE.
Relevance to TRACER: Very close emerging work because it acts after a draft response exists and includes an enhancement path involving a stronger model.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER must not claim that post-response accept/enhance routing is absent. The narrower distinction is explicit action-conditional residual failure estimation for ACCEPT, REPAIR, and independent REGENERATE under a risk-controlled policy.

Paper Title: Conformal Cascade: Distribution-Free Accuracy Guarantees for Multi-Tier LLM Inference
Authors: Yifan Dou; Shikan Fang; Shibo Li
Problem: Replace brittle confidence-threshold cascade decisions with a calibrated rule that provides finite-sample accuracy guarantees.
Dataset / Task Setting: Multi-tier LLM cascades evaluated on multiple-choice benchmarks across several open-weight model families, as reported by the preprint.
Method: Uses conformal prediction-set size as the accept/defer rule; accept when the calibrated set collapses to one answer, otherwise defer to the next tier.
Metrics / Evaluation: Accuracy guarantee/coverage behaviour and cascade cost/acceptance rate.
Key Findings: The preprint reports distribution-free finite-sample accuracy control and improved cascade behaviour over calibration-tuned heuristic thresholds on many evaluated pairs.
Limitations / Conflicting Evidence: Preprint only; action space is accept/defer rather than repair versus independent regeneration. Open-ended generation requires an answer-clustering extension.
Relevance to TRACER: Strongest emerging warning against claiming novelty for calibrated thresholds or risk-controlled acceptance itself.
Gap Evidence / How We Use It: TRACER's contribution must be framed around three action-conditioned residual risks and the repair-vs-regenerate choice, not around conformal/selective thresholding.
